name: Denver
tagline: Mile-High Mountain Living, Craft Beer Culture, and 300 Days of Sunshine
description: Denver sits at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, offering FIRE retirees an unmatched combination of outdoor adventure, urban culture, and over 300 days of sunshine per year. The city has evolved far beyond its frontier roots into a sophisticated metro with a thriving craft beer scene, excellent farm-to-table dining, and world-class skiing just 90 minutes away. Housing costs have climbed significantly in recent years but remain well below coastal cities, and Colorado's flat state income tax keeps the overall tax burden moderate. For anyone who values hiking, biking, skiing, and an active lifestyle, Denver is hard to beat.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – typical for a mid-size US city, improving in many neighborhoods
quickFacts.climate: Continental semi-arid with cold, dry winters and warm summers

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable studio or small 1BR in an outer neighborhood — Montbello, Westwood, or outer Aurora

dining.description: Brewery taprooms and casual eateries; mostly cooking at home

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan through Connect for Health Colorado, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; Colorado's state programs help hold premiums down. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas; RTD light rail for some downtown trips

entertainment.description: Hundreds of free Front Range trails, city parks, free brewery tours

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable studio or small one-bedroom in an outer neighborhood like Montbello or Aurora, where housing plus the car eat more than half the budget. The ACA Silver premium stays affordable only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 subsidy cliff — Colorado's Option plans and reinsurance help hold sticker prices down. The upside is Denver's signature asset: hundreds of free Front Range trails. Ski days are a stretch at this tier, but hiking and biking run most of the year.

housing.description: A decent 1BR in a solid area — Capitol Hill or Baker

dining.description: Dining out several times a week across the RiNo and LoDo scenes; weekend brunch

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost low only if MAGI is managed under the cliff

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage plus an RTD pass and summer bike-share

entertainment.description: Ski day passes at Loveland or A-Basin, Red Rocks concerts, Rockies games, a gym

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable apartment in Capitol Hill or Baker, dining out several times a week in the RiNo scene, Red Rocks concerts in summer, and ski day passes a few times each winter. A reliable car with full coverage is a fixed cost, supplemented by an RTD pass. The budget supports the active, outdoor-oriented life Denver is known for without constant constraint.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR or small 2BR in a walkable district — LoDo, the Highlands, or near Wash Park

dining.description: Regular dining at top tables like Beckon and Guard and Grace

healthcare.description: A Gold plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear

transportation.description: A late-model SUV for mountain trips, premium insurance

entertainment.description: An Ikon Pass for unlimited skiing, Broncos season tickets, premium gym

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality place in LoDo, the Highlands, or near Wash Park, regular dinners at the city's best tables, an Ikon Pass for Copper and Winter Park, and Broncos season tickets. A late-model SUV handles mountain trips year-round, and healthcare is a padded Gold plan near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff. Denver's moderate cost of living versus the coasts means this budget stretches into a genuinely affluent life.

housing.description: A luxury condo in Cherry Creek or Hilltop

dining.description: Fine dining multiple nights a week plus occasional private-chef entertaining

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized premium plan plus concierge medicine at UCHealth

transportation.description: A luxury SUV plus a second vehicle and occasional private car service

entertainment.description: A premium Broncos suite, a country club membership, heli-skiing, arts patronage

domesticHelp.description: Bi-weekly cleaning, landscaping, snow removal, occasional assistant tasks

luxuryExtras.description: Mountain cabin weekends, first-class ski trips, quarterly travel, wine collecting

5M.lifestyle: A luxury condo in Cherry Creek or Hilltop, a housekeeper, and a luxury SUV for weekend runs to Aspen or Telluride. Dining at the best restaurants happens without budgeting, healthcare is unsubsidized concierge care at UCHealth, and business class is standard for longer trips. A country club membership and arts patronage fit comfortably; the coastal-relative discount makes each dollar go further here.

housing.description: A prime-district penthouse or a Cherry Hills Village / Cherry Creek estate rental

dining.description: Private-chef dining and the finest restaurants in the city

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge medicine and executive wellness

transportation.description: A premium vehicle with full ownership costs, plus regular private car service

entertainment.description: Premium club-level Broncos season tickets, heli-skiing, international travel, major arts and hospital philanthropy

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus grounds, snow-removal, and handyman service

luxuryExtras.description: An Aspen or Vail mountain estate, first-class international travel, art collecting, philanthropy

10M.lifestyle: A Cherry Hills Village estate or a prime-district penthouse with mountain views, housekeeping and grounds help several days a week, and occasional private-chef evenings alongside the city's best restaurants. Dining is anywhere, travel is first class, and premium club-level Broncos season tickets come with the territory, alongside major support for the city's arts and hospitals. A second home in Aspen or Vail is feasible; the blend of urban amenities and immediate Rocky Mountain access defines the life at roughly $222k a year.
